clauses.text: Low-friction return: the athlete says they are better, a short check fit to the context, a conservative return when eligible, executed sessions decide how much and when to progress. The window's end, elapsed time or a faster speed never by itself restores prior doses. No daily questionnaire. No watch, exam, certificate or physical test as a condition of any conservative return. A missing record is neither intolerance nor evidence for a progression that needs evidence.
clauses.answers: FP-4 (PCG-V1CP-F02): no speed reaches the held doses because the window ended; a step toward them is admissible only as a step of an approved recipe that executed sessions support, within the caps. Whether sessions executed inside a REDUCE_LIGHT window count as that support is SSCTR mapping.

clauses.text: The three speeds stay: distinct where there is margin, never artificially aggressive, temporary, not the coach profiles.

A registered race stays visible; during an incompatible return it is never automatically considered adequate or authorized. Paths: move/update the date, remove it from the plan, keep the event registered without it becoming a prescription or authorization to compete. When kept, the athlete's decision to take part is separated from the recommendation the coach can sustain. No endless question; a pending race answer never blocks eligible training. Keeping the date never itself ends or shortens a reduction or a return.

The athlete MAY state an early recovery, before the third day included; it opens the short check; it presumes no clinical recovery and MUST NOT bypass a limit, contraindication or restriction in force. The 3-14 days are the reduction chosen at the report, not an obligation.

Warning-sign wording: stop and seek an appropriate professional assessment; for a potentially serious sign, identified from the existing instrument and its criteria, urgent care proportional to the risk; no invented diagnosis, urgency class or clearance; wording that depends on pending G04 authority marked for review before real use; mild indisposition never an emergency.
clauses.answers: the interim urgency-wording item (PCG-V1CP-F03; DR-148 'Open / owner'); final copy stays Product/UX with G03, reviewed by G04 when appointed

clauses.text: Demanding ships as a functionally distinct prescriptive coach only if a real, observable, admissible difference exists (the SSCTR rules); otherwise the limitation is recorded and Demanding is not declared functionally complete nor presented as distinct prescriptive behaviour in V1.
Each of HQ-V1CP-SSCTR-Q01..Q12 receives a traceable disposition; no automatic mission, round or governance step; the human queue stays at 235 unless the Founder appends.

premise.text: A short check plus executed sessions steer a conservative return well enough for training adaptation, and the existing warning-sign instrument identifies the potentially serious signs well enough for interim wording. Not validated; DR-102 revalidation and a future G04 owner.

previous.text: No new dose, threshold, count, length, increment, cadence or percentage unless the SSCTR approves it as a NEW PARAMETER in a separate file with its own decision record; the 3-14 day range is Founder-decided (D2, B1).

new.text: No new dose, threshold, count, length, increment, cadence or percentage unless the SSCTR approves it as a NEW PARAMETER in a separate file with its own decision record. The 3-14 day range is Founder-decided (D2, B1) as the reduction the athlete chooses at the report (DR-149 (4), D4): it is neither an obligation to stay in the reduction nor a minimum time of indisposition. The athlete may end the reduction early, before the third day included, by stating they have recovered; the statement opens the short check, with the clinical screen first (RC-01) and every warning-sign item and restriction the existing instrument requires for that context (an unanswered item is ASK). An early end presumes no clinical recovery, is never a clearance, and never bypasses a limit, a contraindication or a restriction in force (RC-09). The return after it follows the return rules (RC-12, DR-149 (1)) from the window's actual days. An early end never resets the per-sport 14-day count (RC-06 reading). The upper bound stands: a reduction never extends a continuous per-sport window past 14 days without a Founder decision.

readings.subject: D3 against C-Q05-3 (window race question) and the recheck's C-2 modification (window-end race question); the PCG consistency item

sources.C-Q05-3: A window holding the race day asks about the race (keep the date and end the window before it, move it, or skip it); the race is never silently kept or dropped. Inside an R0-R3 window no race-effort touch or quality session is prescribed.
sources.C-2 modified: For a race inside the weeks the return needs, the window-end check offers C-Q05-3's three answers. A race already kept at the window question is not asked again. Keep: the return ends before the race week. The race week, the post-event week and the next block follow the event rules. ... Move or skip: as now. The race keeps waiting during the wait.

reading: Both questions offer the same three paths: move or update the date; remove the race from the plan (C-Q05-3's and C-2's 'skip'); keep the event registered. Consistency holds by giving 'keep' one meaning at both questions: D3's.

D3's keep: the event stays registered and visible; during a return incompatible with it, the engine never treats it as adequate or authorized and never turns it into a prescription or an authorization to compete; the coach's prescription keeps following what the return can sustain; the athlete's decision to take part is recorded as their own, separately from the coach's recommendation, never as a clearance or an authorization.

C-Q05-3's 'keep the date and end the window before it' no longer ties keeping to ending the reduction: keeping never itself ends or shortens a reduction or a return. Ending the reduction early stays available, but only as the athlete's own D4 statement and short check.

C-2's 'Keep: the return ends before the race week. The race week, the post-event week and the next block follow the event rules' does not apply to a return incompatible with the race: cutting the return short so the race week follows the event rules would make the engine treat the race as adequate, which D3 excludes. It still describes the case where the return is compatible with the race; what makes a return compatible, and what the coach recommends around a kept race, is SSCTR mapping (no new number).

No endless question: an answer, once given, stands until the athlete changes it or a fact it rested on changes (the race date, a new report, a clinical route). C-2's 'A race already kept at the window question is not asked again' fits this.

Eligible training is never blocked: while the race answer is pending, the return proceeds for eligible sports and the race is not prescribed; 'the race keeps waiting during the wait' may mean only that the event waits, never that sessions wait (the r12 dead end, SSCTR-V1CPR-02). A clinical hold is not eligible training and still holds.

Scope: D3 speaks of 'uma retomada incompatível'. This reading applies it wherever an F08 path meets a registered race, the reduction window included, because the reduction is the first part of the return (DR-148 (5)); this is the stricter reading and it is flagged INFERRED for the Chief's consolidation.

readings.ruling: NO authority conflict, under these product-level conditions; RC-06 and RC-07 text unchanged.
conditions: Per sport: RC-06 applies to each sport separately. Each sport's continuous Situation 1 reduction is counted from the first window start of the chain that covers it, however many episodes or reports form that chain; an episode over a disjoint sport neither resets nor extends that count. C-1 (d) (the count runs until a whole ladder week has been executed after the window) keeps every continuous per-sport window within 14 days, so no SSCTR exception under RC-06's 'without an explicit SSCTR rule' is used or needed. Any future rule that would extend a continuous per-sport window past 14 days crosses the Founder-decided 3-14 range and goes to the Founder.

Never less conservative: for each sport, the combination of open episodes and a new report is never less conservative than any of them (C-1 principle, RC-13); a later, narrower or lighter report never ends another episode's protection of a sport it does not cover.

Neither an athlete's early end (DR-149 (4)) nor a declared break resets the per-sport count; a declared break is not executed return, so it never counts as the whole executed ladder week that ends a chain.

RC-07: supersession inside Situation 1 (a report over an open Situation 1 episode) is not a conversion between channels. A Situation 1 report and a declared break are never converted into each other: when one supersedes the other's future effect from a date (I-15), each keeps its own type, cause and record (RC-14); nothing is relabelled (R-F08-1). How a break and an open Situation 1 episode combine on one sport is SSCTR content, bounded by 'never less conservative'.
Low friction (D1): with two episodes open, their checks are separate facts but should be presented without repeated questioning (DESIGN_SPACE for Product/UX, SHOULD).
